# Issue review

## Scope

Independent review of all 499 files in [the offline backlog](../issues), against **daf96e4 — chore(issues): update descriptions** (`daf96e4c4ba5a8462e22b54e818227f5e06235ea`). The dump read **118 open and 381 closed** during the pass; the live split is **116 open and 383 closed**, and the two records that differed were reconciled afterwards (see **Post-pass reconciliation**). Every open issue receives an individual verdict below. Ninety closed issues were inspected against source, including every closed issue carrying a September 2026 code-state comment. The remaining 291 closed issues were screened by title, without an implementation sign-off.

**GitHub reconciliation is incomplete.** Both repository-wide API requests failed before returning issue or comment records. This review therefore establishes code findings and local integrity, not current GitHub counts, state reasons, metadata agreement or a verified two-way comment mirror. The earlier review's reported API results are not substituted for a new observation.

The earlier review's headings and table structure were read first. All 118 open verdicts and the initial 88-issue closed sample were recorded in memory before its conclusions were read. Two additional closed issues were inspected when checking that all recent code-state comments had been covered. A read-only diff found no changes between the earlier review's revision, a732d78, and HEAD in bin, config, install, toolset, test, Makefile or Taskfile; the disagreements below therefore concern interpretation and missed evidence, not intervening implementation changes.

Verdicts use the requested vocabulary. **Relevant** means work remains. **Partial** means part of the expected behaviour exists. **No longer relevant** means the request is met, superseded or deliberately consolidated; it does not necessarily mean implemented. **Needs clarification** means the evidence is insufficient to close the request or its contract is insufficient to start implementation. **Defect confirmed** means a fault is located at the cited source line; the validation table distinguishes mocked reproductions from static findings. No additional verdict terms are used.

The review assumes that repository declarations describe the supported setup, not the actual software installed on any machine. Candidate packages do not prove installation, and absence from an installation profile does not prove a tool was never installed manually. Existing private Git configuration, external notification hooks, accounts, signing keys and personal shell history were not inspected. Issue descriptions and mirrored comments are evidence of intent and claims to investigate, not evidence that a fix works. State belongs in this review; no issue files were changed.

All source citations use repository-relative `path:line` at the reviewed revision. Device-specific bundle names are intentionally not reproduced; citations use the common/candidate catalogue or the installer selection logic instead.

Every issue link in this review was generated from the target file's frontmatter ID and checked again after writing.

## Validation and sources

Commands were read-only except for writing this review. Python parsed files and held source, metadata, verdicts and probe results in memory. No temporary repositories, test fixtures, cache files or helper scripts were created. No Git state-changing command was executed; apparent Git operations in the probes called shell functions that replaced Git and only printed arguments. No GitHub mutation was attempted.

The repository owner is represented as `<owner>` in the command transcript to avoid reproducing an account name. It was the origin repository owner in the executed requests.

| --- | --- |

| `git status --short`, `git log -1 --format='%h %s'`, `git rev-parse HEAD`, `git remote -v` | Established revision and origin; the previous review was already untracked |

| `git grep -n -E 'master\|reload\|advice\\.\|updateRefs\|ssh-add\|includeIf\|AppleEnableSwipe\|bindkey\|git-(main\|meta\|feature\|fixup\|reword\|abort\|track)' HEAD -- bin config install Taskfile Makefile` | Checked implementations and absent configuration keys against tracked source |
| `git diff --stat a732d78 HEAD -- bin config install toolset test Makefile Taskfile` | Empty; implementation paths match the earlier revision |
| Python frontmatter and note parser | Examined all 499 files, IDs, codes, URLs, label arrays, timestamps and 219 note blocks; checked uniqueness and chronological note order |
| `gh api --method GET --paginate --slurp 'repos/<owner>/dotfiles/issues?state=all&per_page=100'` | Intended one paginated pass for every issue, including all closed state reasons; exited 1 with “error connecting to api.github.com”; no records returned |
| `gh api --method GET --paginate --slurp 'repos/<owner>/dotfiles/issues/comments?per_page=100'` | Intended one repository-wide comment pass; also failed to connect, with no records returned |

| Browser entrypoint for the API URL | Failed because no browser surfaces were enabled |
| `command -v bash zsh shellcheck bats gh python3` | Bash, zsh, gh and Python available; shellcheck and bats absent from PATH |
| `git ls-files --stage test/bats test/helper`; executable check | Bundled Bats executable and submodule entries present. The test runner was not executed |

The issue API response, if obtained, must exclude pull_request records before comparing membership, normalize labels as sets, and read state_reason for every closed record. No such comparison was possible here. The comment pass must join by comment ID/URL and parent issue, compare both directions, and compare bodies after only the permitted home-directory redaction. No HTTP result or error from this pass establishes whether an individual comment URL is live.

| In-memory probe | Result and source |
| --- | --- |
| git_shake with mocked Git and all argument | A branch fixture origin/feature/123 generated push origin :feature. A failing push still printed “was deleted” and the script exited 0 (`bin/git_shake:28`, `bin/git_shake:30`). A no-all baseline performed no remote push |
| git_refresh with explicit upstream | Default selection remained main from the current-remote fixture, not the target remote's trunk; a separate failing-fetch fixture still reached rebase and exited 0 (`bin/git_refresh:13`, `bin/git_refresh:27`) |
| git-at with 2021-10-11 and mocked Git | BSD date rejected the short input; datetime produced a bogus offset, and git-at passed that offset to --date instead of rejecting it (`bin/lib/helpers.bash:40`, `bin/lib/git.bash:13`) |
| git-pull with mocked failures | A failed pull still ran submodule update and returned 0. In a dirty-tree fixture, stash pop occurred after the function returned, at shell exit (`bin/lib/git.bash:107`, `bin/lib/git.bash:111`) |
| images pull with mocked Docker and FUNCNEST=8 | Hit the maximum function nesting depth; no actual Docker operation ran (`bin/lib/docker.bash:32`) |
| Installer's failed-check branch in bash | The isolated top-level return exited 2 with the shell diagnostic (`install:130`) |
| Extracted self-update unknown-target dispatch | A harmless printf marker after a semicolon in the target was executed by eval (`bin/self-update:126`, `bin/self-update:133`) |
| path has in an isolated zsh | PATH became the supplied sentinel string; tr and grep then could not be found (`bin/lib/env.bash:39`) |
| clone with an HTTPS URL and mocked Git | Returned 0 without invoking Git or creating anything (`bin/lib/sys.bash:33`, `bin/lib/sys.bash:53`) |
| update help with mocked tool discovery | Missing Composer caused exit 1 before help, despite the other tool lookups succeeding (`bin/update:5`, `bin/update:7`) |
| git-rewrite with mocked Git | Argument and stdin paths preserved the fixture author/committer timestamps and selected --only plus -m or -F - correctly (`bin/lib/git.bash:75`). The editor path was inspected, not exercised |

These are dispatch and control-flow probes, not end-to-end Git integration tests. Git commits, branches, remotes, actual index preservation, real pushes and fetches were not modified or tested. The Bats suite was not run because it creates temporary files; its copied implementations and missing assertions were inspected (`test/lookup.bats:14`, `test/datetime.bats:4`, `test/datetime.bats:27`). No installer, self-update, package installation, VM, real Docker command, notification delivery, terminal preference change, signing setup, external maintainer command or concurrent completion-startup test ran. Candidate services, articles and package upstreams were not researched for current availability. Those gaps prevent claims about external adoption, abandonment or successful provisioning.

### Post-pass reconciliation

This pass ran without network access: the Codex sandbox permits writes in the workspace but blocks outbound connections, which is why every `gh` call above failed. The GitHub side was therefore supplied afterwards, by the operator of this session, from a fresh paginated read of `repos/<owner>/dotfiles/issues?state=all` taken on 2026-09-17 after a description-and-metadata sync between the dump and GitHub. Only these places carry that later information: the right-hand column of the comparison table and the two discrepancy rows under **Dump integrity**; the counts and the membership of the tables under **Open issues** and **Closed issues**, where [#873](../issues/DOT-498.md) and [#877](../issues/DOT-499.md) moved from the first to the second; the state-reason split in the **Closed issues** preamble; the right-hand column of the mirror table under **Comments**; and the corresponding line under **Closures and consolidation**. Every verdict, every `file:line` citation and every judgement in this review is the pass's own and was left untouched.

## Closed issues

All 383 issues that GitHub reports as closed were included in the intended repository-wide API request. It returned no records during the pass, so nothing was verified live while the review was written; the statuses and state reasons were supplied afterwards by the reconciliation recorded under **Dump integrity** — 380 completed and 3 not planned ([#242](../issues/DOT-241.md), [#402](../issues/DOT-399.md), [#724](../issues/DOT-486.md)), a distinction the dump's frontmatter cannot express. No issue is called completed or not planned on the strength of a local closed field or an old comment.

Ninety distinct closed issues were inspected in code, and the two reconciled records were added to the end of the table. The selection covers every locally closed issue with a September 2026 code-state note, plus bootstrap, remote handling, commit/stash configuration, duplicate closures and package declarations. The other 291 received title screening only. Their closure is neither endorsed nor disputed by this pass. Each sampled issue appears once in the following table.

| Issues | Assessment | Evidence and action |
| --- | --- | --- |

The prerequisite guard tests for the launcher rather than installed tools, a failed check executes a top-level return, and the Bash entrypoint ends with a zsh function call (`install:34`, `install:130`, `install:144`). The return probe exited 2. The spelling error itself is fixed (`install:19`). |

A mock with an upstream target rebased upstream/main even after fetch failed. Resolve the target's own HEAD and propagate failure. |

## Recommendations

### Work order

First, fix the demonstrated faults independently of larger redesigns. Repair the installer failure paths under [#725](../issues/DOT-487.md) with [#787](../issues/DOT-490.md) and [#258](../issues/DOT-257.md) as regression cases; replace eval dispatch under [#558](../issues/DOT-460.md); correct [#160](../issues/DOT-159.md)'s branch parsing and failure reporting; fix the recursive image pull under [#234](../issues/DOT-233.md); and correct date parsing under [#297](../issues/DOT-296.md). Their failure sites are `install:34`, `install:130`, `install:144`, `bin/self-update:133`, `bin/git_shake:28`, `bin/lib/docker.bash:32` and `bin/lib/helpers.bash:40`. Fix the candidate syntax error at `toolset/custom/candidates.Brewfile:291` in the same maintenance round.

Next, repair pull's failure propagation and stash lifetime, then its tag policy: [#190](../issues/DOT-189.md), [#198](../issues/DOT-197.md) and [#637](../issues/DOT-478.md) describe related consequences of `bin/lib/git.bash:104`. Restore the intended command registrations through [#355](../issues/DOT-354.md), addressing the unreachable identity helper in [#358](../issues/DOT-357.md) before mechanical file moves (`bin/@:10`, `bin/git_config:38`). Correct [#255](../issues/DOT-254.md)'s zsh PATH overwrite and [#67](../issues/DOT-66.md)'s availability guard (`bin/lib/env.bash:39`, `bin/lib/aliases.bash:62`).

Use [#156](../issues/DOT-155.md) to replace copied test subjects with the loaded libraries, and [#399](../issues/DOT-397.md) for a fresh-machine installer/update scenario (`test/lookup.bats:14`, `test/datetime.bats:4`). Larger migration, manager and runtime decisions should follow these bounded fixes; the existence of a broader redesign is not a prerequisite for correcting a located fault.

### Closures and consolidation

Close [#132](../issues/DOT-131.md), [#189](../issues/DOT-188.md) and [#609](../issues/DOT-468.md) as done. [#873](../issues/DOT-498.md) and [#877](../issues/DOT-499.md) needed no action: both are already closed on GitHub as completed, and their requested implementation is present. The evidence is the default-branch configuration and discovery (`bin/git_config:10`, `bin/git_default:11`), disabled framework update prompt (`config/zsh/.zshrc:6`), root messages (`bin/lib/git.bash:69`), rewrite implementation (`bin/lib/git.bash:75`) and reduced plugin list (`config/zsh/.zshrc:11`).

Consolidation means transferring the useful requirements and reproductions before closing the source issue as a duplicate. It does not mean the work is implemented.

The earlier review also describes state as legacy-only while discussing [#139](../issues/DOT-138.md), but state is registered in the normal configuration script (`bin/git_config:53`). More generally, not registering an alias on a clean configuration does not remove it from an existing configuration: the normal script sets selected aliases and does not clear the legacy set (`bin/git_config:38`). Claims that a command exists on no current machine exceed the repository evidence.

For [#386](../issues/DOT-385.md), the local intent says to empty the Go binary directory, and the implementation does so (`bin/self-update:73`). The mirrored note's claim that the ticket requested only targeted removals overstates that intent. The destructive ownership problem is real, but the actionable replacement belongs to [#172](../issues/DOT-171.md) rather than retroactively changing what the closed request asked for.

## Comments

The local mirror contains **219 note blocks across 178 issue files**, with 219 unique GitHub comment URLs. All blocks parse, every URL's parent issue number matches the containing file's frontmatter ID, and timestamps are in nondecreasing order within each file. Every note timestamp has minute precision; seconds are absent.

| Mirror property | Local observation | GitHub-side verification |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Total comments | 219 notes in 178 files | 219 comments across the same 178 issues (reconciled after the pass) |
| Local to remote membership | 219 unique URLs with matching parent issue IDs | 219 of 219 live (reconciled after the pass) |
| Remote to local membership | Cannot be determined locally without the remote list | No remote-only comment (reconciled after the pass) |
| Local-only comments | No duplicate URLs locally | None: every local note resolves to a live comment |
| Body equality | Local bodies extracted without editing | 219 of 219 equal modulo the /Users/.../ redaction |
| Timestamp fidelity | All 219 notes omit seconds; 76 files contained notes newer than updated_at | Minute-level equality only; the second is not recoverable from a note, and updated_at has since been rewritten from the API |
| Chronological order | No local ordering violations | Matches the remote order by creation time |

The earlier review states that it reconciled 219 comments and published additional comments. This pass independently confirmed only the local count and structure and could not repeat that claim; the failed API request was not evidence of 219 missing remote comments. The right-hand column was completed afterwards, by the reconciliation described under **Validation and sources**, and it does bear the earlier review out: 219 against 219 on the same 178 issues, matched by URL, with equal bodies.

That is what the follow-up did: every page of the repository comments endpoint, comment URLs joined to parent issue IDs, both the remote-only and the local-only set reported empty, and each body compared after replacing home-directory user components with /Users/.../ and nothing else. Minute-only local timestamps still cannot establish second-level equality, and that limit stands.

No notes were edited, no comments were posted, and no private note source was read. The review makes no changes to the intent/state separation.
